record.paper_title: Cyber-Physical Attacks on UAS Networks–Challenges and Open Research Problems
record.context_brief: Proactive spoofing-signal elimination for UAV navigation
record.original_question: Can proactive mechanisms that eliminate spoofing signals be made applicable to UAV sensory and navigation subsystems, and what design would make those mechanisms robust under the speed and spatial freedom of UAVs rather than relying only on reactive detection of navigation attacks?

evidence.quote: Since the establishment of GPS, various countermeasures against GNSS spoofing have been proposed, ranging from exploitation of direction and polarization of the received GPS signal for attack detection to beamforming and statistical signal processing methods for elimination of spoofing signals [6]. However, the speed and spatial freedom of UAVs render many of the basic assumptions and criteria of such techniques inapplicable.

Robustness of the sensory and navigational subsystem against spoofing attacks may be further improved by implementation of proactive mechanisms through elimination of spoofing signals, applicability of which to UAVs is yet to be investigated.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) equipped with a Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver used for navigation. A spoofing attack is modeled as the injection, at the receiver's antenna, of one or more counterfeit GNSS-like signals s_a(t) superimposed on the authentic satellite signals s_l(t), so that the received baseband signal has the form r(t) = Σ_l s_l(t − τ_l) e^{j 2π f_{D,l} t} + Σ_a s_a(t − τ_a) e^{j 2π f_{D,a} t} + n(t), where τ, f_D denote propagation delay and Doppler shift and n(t) is additive noise. Classical proactive spoofing-elimination methods (e.g., antenna-array beamforming that places nulls in the direction of arrival of the spoofer, polarization-based filtering, and statistical signal-processing cancellation) typically rely on assumptions that include: (i) approximately stationary or slowly moving receiver; (ii) stable antenna orientation enabling reliable direction-of-arrival or polarization estimates; (iii) limited angular dynamics of the receiver relative to legitimate satellites. A UAV violates these assumptions because of its high translational and angular velocity and large spatial freedom (six degrees of freedom, rapid attitude changes, possibly long mission radius).

Problem. Design a proactive on-board mechanism that suppresses or cancels spoofing components from r(t) before the navigation solution is computed (rather than merely detecting their presence) and that satisfies all of the following:
1. Operates in real time on a moving platform whose linear speed v and angular rate ω may take values within prescribed UAV operational ranges.
2. Does not require the receiver to be quasi-stationary or to maintain a fixed antenna attitude.
3. Provides a quantifiable robustness guarantee: for a specified spoofer power-advantage range and a specified set of admissible UAV trajectories, the post-cancellation residual spoofing power is bounded below a threshold that preserves correct acquisition and tracking of the authentic signals.
4. Is implementable with sensors and computation feasible on a UAV (e.g., small antenna array, onboard IMU aiding).

Either exhibit such a mechanism together with a proof (analytical or rigorous performance bounds) of properties (1)–(4), or prove that no mechanism in a specified class can simultaneously satisfy them under the given UAV mobility model.
artifact.category_tag: GNSS anti-spoofing signal processing for UAVs
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys and recent work on GNSS anti-spoofing for UAVs (2020–2025) continue to emphasize detection-oriented techniques and report that proactive cancellation methods (beamforming nulls, polarization filtering, spatial processing) face open challenges when transferred to highly mobile UAV platforms. No general proactive elimination scheme with robustness guarantees under arbitrary UAV speed and attitude dynamics has been established; the question remains an active area of research.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on GPS/GNSS Spoofing and Anti-Spoofing Techniques for UAVs
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews GNSS spoofing countermeasures and lists open challenges for UAV platforms, where high mobility limits applicability of array-based and polarization-based mitigation.
status_evidence.claim: Proactive cancellation for UAVs is identified as an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: GNSS Spoofing Detection and Mitigation: A Review
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses beamforming, polarization, and statistical cancellation techniques and notes their reliance on quasi-static receiver assumptions, hindering UAV deployment.
status_evidence.claim: Existing proactive elimination methods are not yet robust to UAV mobility.
